description:
Is There a Hidden Planet You've Never Seen?

Episode 51 of a daily journey through the universe. 🪐
Planet Nine: since 2016 astronomers have argued that the strangely lined-up orbits of distant icy objects point to an unseen planet several times Earth's mass, far beyond Neptune. Others disagree. The Vera Rubin Observatory may settle it.

#space #planetnine #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: What if there's a whole planet in our solar system that nobody has ever seen?
Far beyond Neptune, there are small icy worlds circling the Sun on huge, stretched-out orbits.
segments.headline: Beyond Neptune

segments.text: In twenty sixteen, two astronomers, Konstantin Batygin and Mike Brown, noticed something odd. Several of these orbits seemed to point in the same direction.
segments.headline: Lined-up orbits

segments.text: They calculated the chance of that happening by luck was very small.
Their idea: a hidden planet, several times heavier than Earth, is herding them with its gravity.
segments.headline: A hidden planet?

segments.text: It would be so far away that it could take ten thousand years or more to orbit the Sun once.
So far out, it would reflect very little sunlight. That's why no one has seen it.
segments.headline: Too dark to see

segments.text: Not everyone agrees. Some say the pattern comes from where telescopes happened to look. Others think a disk of small objects could do it.
segments.headline: Others disagree

segments.text: The answer may come soon. The new Vera Rubin Observatory in Chile is scanning the whole southern sky again and again.
segments.headline: Rubin is watching

segments.text: If it's out there, Planet Nine would be the first new planet found in our solar system since Neptune, in eighteen forty-six.
segments.headline: First since 1846?

segments.text: Next stop: The Oort Cloud. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for the next stop.
